benchmark: Nifty 50 index price series from Yahoo Finance; not a total-return benchmark

data_quality.message: Data-quality gate passed: 50 stock histories downloaded, 50 with at least 300 daily bars, and 1236 benchmark bars. The report evaluates up to 756 recent sessions (about 3 years), with calendar-year checks. Coverage checks do not guarantee accuracy or predict future performance.

data_source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance; research-only and may be delayed, incomplete, or unavailable

research_methodology.benchmark: Each strategy is compared against Nifty 50 price-index close-to-close return over the same sample.
research_methodology.candidate_policy: Candidates are research-only and never automatically replace the active strategy.
research_methodology.cost_model: Configured transaction costs and adverse slippage are included; each candidate also receives 1.5x and 2.0x cost stress checks.
research_methodology.fill_timing: Signals calculated after the close; target orders fill at next session open.
limitations: Current index constituents introduce survivorship bias.
Yahoo Finance data is unofficial and may be revised or incomplete.
A three-year window and one set of historical constituents cannot establish future profitability.
Trying many variants can overfit; judge robustness and later paper-trading, not the best single return.
The cost stress multiplies both modeled transaction costs and slippage; it does not model market impact or liquidity constraints.
research_methodology.robustness_checks: Each fixed strategy is re-tested over 252-, 504-, and 756-session windows, plus 1.5x and 2.0x transaction-cost/slippage scenarios. These overlapping windows are sensitivity checks, not independent validation.
research_methodology.walk_forward_checks: Each strategy is tested on four consecutive 126-session chronological folds with no overlap between return intervals. Each fold uses a fresh simulated portfolio; results are not one compounded equity curve and do not prove future profitability.
research_methodology.yearly_breakdown: Calendar-year sub-periods from the same continuous simulation; partial first/last years are possible.

results.methodology: Signals use data available through each close; target orders fill at next session open with configured costs/slippage. The normal permanent 10% drawdown lock remains in force; after it triggers, the simulation stays in cash.

robustness.interpretation: Sensitivity checks only, not independent out-of-sample proof. Periods overlap, the universe has survivorship bias, and the benchmark excludes dividends.

walk_forward.interpretation: Chronological fixed-rule validation on consecutive, non-overlapping test periods. The strategy is not re-tuned between folds; each fold starts with a fresh simulated portfolio, so this is not a single deployable compounded equity curve and does not prove future profitability.

A small number of historical windows does not establish future profitability.
Nifty is a price-index benchmark, the constituent universe has survivorship bias, and market-data quality can vary.
This is a research-only policy comparison, not permission to place real-money orders.
risk_recovery_comparison.methodology: Both policies use the same active strategy and market data. The recovery overlay remains in cash after a drawdown lock until Nifty closes below its 200-session SMA and then later closes back above it, with at least one eligible target and a valid next-open price. Re-entry happens at the next open; the risk reference peak resets to re-entry equity. The scheduled paper trader and its permanent lock are not changed.

selection_note: Research includes the existing momentum rules, classic 12-1 relative strength, 6/12-month dual momentum, and a Nifty 200-day regime filter. Research never auto-promotes candidates. Current constituents create survivorship bias; metrics are not forecasts. Paper-trial candidates separately before considering promotion.
